answer: Identity mills jam at a one-flue smelter. A key bonds 1.19 POA for one flue tagged with a public 21-byte ash hash. Over 15 hours it must raise one exhaust plume and five whisper pulses, each a 16-byte tick signed 88 minutes apart from a fresh /24 and bound to the ash hash plus the live tip. Three tundra wardens recompute every tick and reject a reused /16 or two ticks closer than 75 minutes. If four flues ignite under one wallet in 11 hours, or two flues share three tick prefixes, all go cold and the 1.19 POA stays slagged. A missed pulse leaves the flue uncertified; no second flue is lit.
